title: Four Mile Creek Flipbook
h1: Four Mile Creek aerial flipbook, 1942 to 2025
sub: APN 104-144-018 (123 ac) and the 3,333 ac Fourmile Creek watershed, which drains west to the Pacific south of the Mattole River mouth
notes:
What this covers

Nineteen dates, February 1942 to May 2025. Every frame is on the same UTM zone 10N grid, so the flip is registered. The watershed view is 9 by 4.05 km at 1.5 m per pixel and takes in the ridges on both sides of Fourmile Creek. The parcel view is 1.32 km square at 0.4 m per pixel.

1942 through 1981 are full-resolution scans. These eight dates are mosaics of scanned prints from Cal Poly Humboldt, about 0.5 to 1 m per pixel at source. I orthorectified each frame against the 10 m 3DEP elevation model, then tightened each year against the next later year, ending at 1993 and 2005 NAIP. Offsets between adjacent years are a few metres, more on steep ground. Seams show where flight lines meet, tone differs between prints, and some prints carry grease-pencil lines. Black areas have no frame for that year. Several years stop short of the beach on the west side.

1993 is two USGS frames at about 1.7 m. Chips with dashed borders mark black-and-white dates.

Color balance varies by year in the NAIP frames and I left the tones as delivered. Canopy texture, openings and road lines are the reliable signal.

3D views. Each year is draped on the 10 m elevation model and rendered from four fixed cameras: the parcel from the south, the watershed from above the surf looking east, the full length of the watershed from the south, and the watershed from above the headwaters looking west. The terrain model is smooth at this resolution, so gullies and road cuts do not show as relief, and steep slopes stretch the photos somewhat. Grey terrain has no photo coverage for that year.

Gaps. I found no usable frames between 1981 and 1993, none from 1958, and could not place the 1974 frames. No 2024 NAIP image was available for this area, so the sequence steps from July 2022 to the May 2025 satellite image. The 1981 flight is missing the line over the middle of the watershed.

Parcel boundary is from Humboldt County GIS. The watershed divide is delineated from the 10 m elevation model above the creek mouth. Stream lines are from the National Hydrography Dataset, which names the creek Fourmile Creek. None of these lines is a survey.

Fire record. The optional fire layer shows CAL FIRE historical perimeters. The Beatty Escape Fire of October 16, 1960 (5,720 acres) is mapped across the whole parcel and about 3,150 acres of the 3,333 acre watershed, so the 1959 and 1963 frames bracket it. The 1964 Mattole Fire perimeter takes in about 74 acres of the watershed. A perimeter drawn dashed burned after the date on screen. Older perimeters were often sketched by hand at coarse scale, and the record misses small and early fires, so treat edges as approximate.

Canopy height, legacy trees and wetness index

These three layers are off when the page opens. Turn them on in the legend and set their transparency with the opacity slider. They are available in the watershed, parcel and 3D views and do not change with the date on screen.

Canopy height is from the 2018 USGS 3DEP LiDAR survey: highest return minus the LiDAR ground surface on a 1 m grid. Ground under 2 m of cover is left clear.

Legacy trees are LiDAR canopy tops at least 131 ft (40 m) tall with a full crown around the top, the same screen used in the timber survey. It flags 51 tops inside the parcel and 1,557 in the watershed. This is a remote screen and not a cruise. Heights are as of 2018, a top on a steep slope can read tall, and a tree lost since 2018 still shows.

Topographic Wetness Index is ln(a / tan β), computed from the 10 m elevation model with D-infinity flow routing. It shows where terrain concentrates drainage: swales, hollows and valley floors. It is not a measurement of soil moisture, and at 10 m it does not resolve road drainage or small gullies.
